A.why: A wide steel kettle-hat brim gives a distinct top-down silhouette and a believable watchman, but the navy and brown sink in the dark and cream is almost absent.
A.fix: Put cream or town-blue heraldry on the pauldron tops and the hat crown so the town colours read before the steel.

B.why: The colours are clean and apart from the references, but the kepi, white belt and chevron read as a modern policeman, not a gothic garrison.
B.fix: Replace the peaked cap with a brimmed steel cap or blue coif and move the heraldry onto the pauldron tops.

C.why: From above it is a grey bucket helm and grey slab pauldrons, which reads as the iron family despite the good blue-and-cream tabard.
C.fix: Paint the pauldron tops and helm in town blue with cream edging so the ARPG read is blue-and-cream, not grey.

D.why: The quartered blue-and-cream torso and the cream cross on the cap crown are the clearest heraldic family read from the high camera.
D.fix: Give the charcoal pauldrons a blue face with cream or brass edging and add the missing brass badge.

E.why: The blue coif fits the gothic world, but the promised pavise does not show and one odd pale pauldron is the only bright shape.
E.fix: Hang a broad blue-and-cream pavise on the back as the one silhouette idea and balance or recolour the lone pauldron.

F.why: Crested sallet, cream-edged pauldrons and a brass chest roundel meet the brief most fully, but the helm reads as a pale grey box from above.
F.fix: Widen the plume into a blue-and-cream front-to-back crest or blue the helm crown so the head reads from the ARPG camera.

notes: D and F are close: D wins on top-down heraldic read (quartering, crown cross), F on fantasy and brass badge. Common weakness across the run: heraldry sits on the chest front where the high camera never looks; the pauldron tops and helm crown should carry the town colours. Several sets lean on grey steel at the top of the silhouette and drift toward iron.
